edits.old: High host memory use alone does not prove a MongoDB memory leak: WiredTiger has an internal cache, the operating system caches files, and other operations consume RAM. Alibaba also documents heap fragmentation as a cause of increasing memory use. In a soak test, separate these categories before interpreting a rising total as leaked allocations. (high confidence)
edits.new: High host memory use alone does not prove a MongoDB memory leak: WiredTiger has an internal cache, the operating system uses free RAM for the filesystem cache, and other processes consume RAM. Alibaba Cloud also documents that the tcmalloc allocator keeps freed request buffers in its own cache instead of returning them to the OS immediately, which can add up to tens of gigabytes. In a soak test, separate these categories before interpreting a rising total as leaked allocations. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/wiredtiger/ ; https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/mongodb/user-guide/troubleshoot-high-memory-usage-on-an-apsaradb-for-mongodb-instance

edits.old: Minimum oplog retention can preserve more history under fluctuating writes, but it can increase disk consumption. A test that enables a retention floor must also observe free disk space; retention time and fixed storage capacity cannot both be assumed constant. (medium confidence)
edits.new: A minimum oplog retention period (storage.oplogMinRetentionHours) makes mongod remove an oplog entry only if the oplog has reached its maximum size and the entry is older than the configured number of hours, so history is preserved for at least that long. The oplog can then grow without constraint to retain entries for the configured hours, which may reduce or exhaust system disk space under high write volume and a large retention period, and mongod may keep that disk space after the oplog shrinks. A test that enables a retention floor should therefore monitor free disk space. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-oplog.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/replsetresizeoplog.md

edits.rationale: MongoDB docs state that with a minimum retention period the oplog is truncated only when it exceeds max size and the entry is older than the configured hours, and that it can grow without constraint, risking disk exhaustion under high write volume. The 'fluctuating writes' framing is not in the sources; the documented risk is high write volume combined with a large retention period. The recommendation to observe free disk space is a sound inference from the documented risk, not a sourced statement.
